cellRule: Every operation x host x profile cell is owned (exactly one producer node and one receiving acceptance ID) or a truthful exclusion with a reason. claimBasis is none for every cell at ratification (WDX0): a cell becomes a support claim only through runtime-observation evidence from AST9 (AST9-AC1) and promotion at AST10 (AST10-AC1). No cell cites ASTP, an installed parser, an installed oracle or syntax highlighting (AST1G) as product evidence.

parserDecision.home: H01 crates/verter_astro_syntax (created by REG0, filled by AST1)

carrier.sublanguage: Astro carrier: frontmatter fence, HTML-shaped markup, components, fragments, expression and attribute islands, directives, script and style element boundaries, comments
rationale:
The carrier's distinguishing structure is not WHATWG tokenization: { } expression islands appear in text and attribute positions and nest markup inside JavaScript ({items.map((i) =>
  • {i}
    • )}), so the tokenizer must hand exact extents to OXC and re-enter markup inside them; attribute shorthand {attr}, spread {...props} and backtick attribute values are carrier syntax; the --- frontmatter fence precedes the template.

The candidate fork source H08 crates/verter_html_syntax does not exist at the described head and is not an ancestor of AST1 in the plan; AST1 rescopes if the decision would fork the tokenizer inside HWC1.
PAR0 PD06 forbids a shared HTML-family parser, recovery mode or cache key, so a fork could not share HWC1's recovery anyway; Astro owns its recovery corpus (AST1-AC2).

lineage.sourceOwner: none (new parser; no in-repository source is copied)
lineage.upstreamSpecification: Astro syntax reference for astro 7.3.8 (docs.astro.build: Astro syntax, Components, Template expressions reference, Directives reference)
lineage.oracle: @astrojs/compiler-rs 0.5.1, test-only grammar oracle; @astrojs/astro2tsx 0.1.2 is the separate test-only projection oracle. Exact pins and upstream dependency ranges are recorded separately in the version lock.

corpus.name: AST0 Astro grammar corpus
corpus.digestRule: sha256 over the sorted lines '<path relative to the corpus>:<hex sha256 of the LF-normalized file bytes>', each line LF-terminated; the validator (AST1G-ACV) recomputes it, and a mismatch means the corpus changed without amending this lock
receivers: AST1-AC1 (lossless round trip over every valid file)
